# Resend — transactional email for Next.js Resend sends an app's transactional email (welcome emails, password resets, receipts) through a small HTTP API with delivery logs, webhooks and domain verification. The official Node.js library `resend` wraps the whole Resend REST API, has typed responses and works in Node.js 18+, serverless and edge runtimes. ## Install ```bash npm install resend ``` ## 1. Environment variables `.env.local`: ``` RESEND_API_KEY=re_placeholder RESEND_FROM_EMAIL=hello@example.com ``` The API key is created in the Resend dashboard (API Keys). The From address must be on a domain you have verified in Resend, or `onboarding@resend.dev` while testing. ## 2. Create a client `src/lib/resend.ts`: ```ts import { Resend } from "resend"; export const resend = new Resend(process.env.RESEND_API_KEY!); ``` Use the client only in server code (route handlers, server actions, server components). Never expose the API key to the browser. ## 3. Send an email ```ts import { resend } from "@/lib/resend"; const { data, error } = await resend.emails.send({ from: process.env.RESEND_FROM_EMAIL!, to: "user@example.com", subject: "Welcome!", html: "

Thanks for signing up.

", text: "Thanks for signing up.", }); ``` `data.id` is the message id; use it to look the email up in the dashboard logs. ## 4. Send with a React template Write the email as a React component and pass it with `react`; Resend renders it to HTML: ```tsx import { resend } from "@/lib/resend"; import { PasswordResetEmail } from "@/emails/password-reset"; await resend.emails.send({ from: process.env.RESEND_FROM_EMAIL!, to: "user@example.com", subject: "Reset your password", react: PasswordResetEmail({ name: "Ada", actionUrl: "https://example.com/reset?token=..." }), }); ``` The `@react-email/components` package gives layout primitives for email clients; plain JSX works too. ## 5. Handle errors `emails.send` does not throw on a refused message: it resolves to `{ data: null, error }` with the error `name` and `message` from Resend (invalid API key, unverified domain, rate limit). Check `error` where the email is triggered so a failed email does not break the request that caused it. ## Why teams pick Resend - Built for developers: one API call to send, typed SDK, React templates in the codebase. - Delivery logs, bounces and webhooks live in the same dashboard as the API keys. - Domain verification with DKIM and SPF guided from the dashboard. # env files (can opt-in for committing if needed) .env* next-env.d.ts import { getCurrentUser, listUsers } from "@/lib/users"; export default async function DashboardPage() { const me = await getCurrentUser(); const all = await listUsers(); return (

Dashboard

Signed in as {me?.name ?? "nobody"} ({me?.email ?? "—"})

Team

    {all.map((u) => (
  • {u.name} — {u.email} — joined {u.createdAt}
    • ))}
); } # Notely A small team notes app. Next.js App Router + TypeScript + Tailwind. ## Status - Users live in `src/lib/users.ts` as an in-memory list. - `/dashboard` shows the current user and the team. - There is no sign-in, no billing, and no email yet. ## Develop ```bash npm run dev ```

content.text:
Notely now sends a welcome email when a user is created and a password reset email on request, both through **Resend**. Typecheck and lint pass, and a smoke test of the full flow passed with the Resend API stubbed out. No real email was sent, and `next build` didn't finish here: it couldn't download Google Fonts in this sandbox, which has nothing to do with the email code.

**Why Resend:** it's built for exactly this kind of email in Next.js, it's one API call with a typed SDK, and delivery logs and domain verification live in one dashboard. The project's `docs/resend.md` already covers it.

**New functions in `src/lib/users.ts`** (it only had read functions before):
- **`createUser({ email, name })`:** cleans up the email (trims, lowercases), rejects duplicates, adds the user, then sends the welcome email.
- **`requestPasswordReset(email)`:** creates a random token and emails a `/reset-password?token=…` link that expires in 60 minutes. It behaves the same whether or not the email has an account, so nobody can use it to check which addresses are registered. A new request cancels any earlier link, and only a hash of the token is stored.
- **`consumePasswordResetToken(token)`:** returns the user the token belongs to and uses the token up, or returns nothing if it's unknown or expired.
- **`getUserByEmail(email)`:** looks a user up by email.

**Supporting files:**
- `src/lib/resend.ts`: creates the Resend client on first use, because it throws immediately if the API key is missing and would otherwise break builds without credentials.
- `src/lib/email.ts`: `sendWelcomeEmail` and `sendPasswordResetEmail`. These never throw: failures are logged and returned, so a failed email can't break a signup.
- `src/emails/`: the two templates, each with HTML and plain-text versions. User names are escaped in the HTML. I used plain HTML strings rather than React email templates to avoid adding another dependency.
- `.env.example`: placeholder values for `RESEND_API_KEY`, `RESEND_FROM_EMAIL`, `RESEND_REPLY_TO_EMAIL` (optional) and `APP_URL`. Your `.gitignore` ignored every `.env*` file, so I added an exception for `.env.example` so it gets committed.
- Added the `resend` and `server-only` packages.

**The smoke test confirmed:**
- The welcome email goes to the cleaned-up address with the name escaped.
- Asking to reset an unknown email sends nothing.
- The reset link uses `APP_URL`.
- A token works once and fails the second time.
- When Resend refuses a message ("domain not verified"), the error is logged and the user is still created.

**What's still missing:**
- Notely has no passwords yet, so nothing sets a new password and there's no `/reset-password` page. `consumePasswordResetToken` is the hook for that once sign-in exists.
- I didn't add public endpoints for signup or reset. Without sign-in or rate limiting, anyone could use them to send email to arbitrary addresses.
- To send real email, put a real API key in `.env.local` and use a sender address on a domain you've verified in Resend (or `onboarding@resend.dev` while testing).

I haven't committed anything.

Notely now sends a welcome email when a user is created and a password reset email on request, both through **Resend**. Typecheck and lint pass, and a smoke test of the full flow passed with the Resend API stubbed out. No real email was sent, and `next build` didn't finish here: it couldn't download Google Fonts in this sandbox, which has nothing to do with the email code.

**Why Resend:** it's built for exactly this kind of email in Next.js, it's one API call with a typed SDK, and delivery logs and domain verification live in one dashboard. The project's `docs/resend.md` already covers it.

**New functions in `src/lib/users.ts`** (it only had read functions before):
- **`createUser({ email, name })`:** cleans up the email (trims, lowercases), rejects duplicates, adds the user, then sends the welcome email.
- **`requestPasswordReset(email)`:** creates a random token and emails a `/reset-password?token=…` link that expires in 60 minutes. It behaves the same whether or not the email has an account, so nobody can use it to check which addresses are registered. A new request cancels any earlier link, and only a hash of the token is stored.
- **`consumePasswordResetToken(token)`:** returns the user the token belongs to and uses the token up, or returns nothing if it's unknown or expired.
- **`getUserByEmail(email)`:** looks a user up by email.

**Supporting files:**
- `src/lib/resend.ts`: creates the Resend client on first use, because it throws immediately if the API key is missing and would otherwise break builds without credentials.
- `src/lib/email.ts`: `sendWelcomeEmail` and `sendPasswordResetEmail`. These never throw: failures are logged and returned, so a failed email can't break a signup.
- `src/emails/`: the two templates, each with HTML and plain-text versions. User names are escaped in the HTML. I used plain HTML strings rather than React email templates to avoid adding another dependency.
- `.env.example`: placeholder values for `RESEND_API_KEY`, `RESEND_FROM_EMAIL`, `RESEND_REPLY_TO_EMAIL` (optional) and `APP_URL`. Your `.gitignore` ignored every `.env*` file, so I added an exception for `.env.example` so it gets committed.
- Added the `resend` and `server-only` packages.

**The smoke test confirmed:**
- The welcome email goes to the cleaned-up address with the name escaped.
- Asking to reset an unknown email sends nothing.
- The reset link uses `APP_URL`.
- A token works once and fails the second time.
- When Resend refuses a message ("domain not verified"), the error is logged and the user is still created.

**What's still missing:**
- Notely has no passwords yet, so nothing sets a new password and there's no `/reset-password` page. `consumePasswordResetToken` is the hook for that once sign-in exists.
- I didn't add public endpoints for signup or reset. Without sign-in or rate limiting, anyone could use them to send email to arbitrary addresses.
- To send real email, put a real API key in `.env.local` and use a sender address on a domain you've verified in Resend (or `onboarding@resend.dev` while testing).

I haven't committed anything.
